title: rust-codemap trace entry event
description: One JSON-Lines record for a span's own NEW event, as produced by the exact tracing_subscriber setup mandated in README.md's "Tracing log format" -- one such record per span, emitted the moment that span is entered. There is no 'formatVersion' field by design (see PROJECT.md §4, "Trace-format schema"): this schema file IS the version -- a real format change edits this file, trace-close.schema.json, both parsers (trace_log.py and the viewer's parseTraceJsonl fallback), and the README snippet together, in one commit.

timestamp.description: tracing_subscriber's own RFC 3339 timestamp. Not read by trace_log.py today (spans are ordered by their position in the file, not by this field) -- documented because it's always present in real output, not because the parser depends on it.

level.description: e.g. "INFO". Not read by trace_log.py -- documented for completeness, same reasoning as timestamp.

fields.description: On an entry event, this is always exactly {"message": "new"} -- tracing_subscriber's own fixed marker for a NEW span event. A span's own captured arguments (e.g. #[instrument]'s a/b for add(a, b)) live inside `span` below, NOT here -- do not confuse the two `fields`-shaped objects in this format.

target.description: The Rust module path tracing_subscriber attributes this event to (e.g. "dcore::basics"). Not read by trace_log.py -- span-to-node resolution uses `filename`/`line_number` instead (see README.md's "How a span is matched to a graph node"), specifically because a module path alone can't disambiguate two crates sharing a module name the way a real file path can.

filename.description: Absolute path to the source file containing the #[instrument] attribute that produced this span. Required, not optional: the mandated main() snippet always sets .with_file(true), and file+line resolution (this field, plus line_number below) is the ONLY way trace_log.py can tell two crates' identically-named default-instrumented spans apart -- see PROJECT.md's cross-crate node-id collision entry in §2.3/§4.

line_number.description: The line the #[instrument] attribute itself starts on -- NOT the fn/method line (see README.md: trace_log.py scans forward from here to find the real item line). Required for the same reason as filename.

span.description: This span's own name plus whatever fields #[instrument] captured as arguments (e.g. {"a": 1, "b": 2} for add(a, b)) or the custom `values` field #[instrument] emits for a Vec/non-Copy argument -- both siblings of `name`, not nested under it. `name` alone is required; every other key is call-site-specific and therefore unconstrained here.

name.description: The span's default (bare fn/method name) or custom (#[instrument(name = "...")]) label. NOT trusted as this tool's node-id match key by itself -- see README.md's "How a span is matched to a graph node" for why (a method's default name is never qualified with its Type, two crates' functions can share the exact same default name, and a custom name can be anything at all).

spans.description: The ordered ancestor chain at the moment this span was entered, root first, EXCLUDING this span itself. An empty array means this is itself a root span (nothing else was open around it, e.g. `main` in a binary). Each element only ever carries a bare `name` (and whatever fields that ancestor's own instrumentation captured) -- never its own filename/line_number, since those would be redundant with that same ancestor's own top-level entry event elsewhere in the trace. trace_log.py, notably, does NOT resolve node ids from this array's text at all (see trace_log.py's own module docstring) -- it reconstructs the real ancestor chain from an internally-tracked open-span stack instead, specifically because two different crates' spans can share an identical bare name here with no way to tell them apart from the text alone.

threadId.description: Optional -- only present with `.with_thread_ids(true)` (see README.md's "Optional: telling concurrent calls apart"). trace_log.py uses this to keep a SEPARATE open-span stack per thread, so two threads' interleaved NEW events never get wrongly nested inside each other. Does not, on its own, reconstruct which thread spawned which -- that needs the target code to explicitly propagate `tracing::Span::current()` across `thread::spawn`, which this project does not require.

threadName.description: Optional -- only present with `.with_thread_names(true)`, alongside threadId above. Not read by trace_log.py for any resolution logic (threadId alone is the grouping key) -- purely informational, e.g. for display.
